cards.title: Aaronson–Ambainis conjecture
cards.area: Communication complexity and Boolean function analysis
cards.formal:
Does there exist a positive integer \(C\) such that for every integer \(n\ge1\), every integer \(1\le d\le n\), and every real multilinear polynomial \(f\) in \(n\) variables of degree at most \(d\),
\[\bigl[\forall x\in\{-1,1\}^n,\ 0\le f(x)\le1\bigr]\quad\Longrightarrow\quad\exists i\in[n]:\ \operatorname{Inf}_i(f)\ge\left(\frac{\operatorname{Var}(f)}d\right)^C?\]
Variance and squared \(L_2\) influence use the uniform distribution on the entire Boolean cube, with the normalization below. The same exponent \(C\) must work for all dimensions, degrees, coefficients and variances.
cards.definitions:
Polynomials and domain. Write \([n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}\) and \(\chi_S(x)=\prod_{j\in S}x_j\) for \(S\subseteq[n]\), with \(\chi_{\varnothing}=1\). A real multilinear polynomial is a finite sum
\[f(x)=\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}a_S\chi_S(x),\qquad a_S\in\mathbb R.\]
Multilinear means that each variable has exponent at most one in each monomial. Degree at most \(d\) means \(a_S=0\) whenever \(|S|>d\). The range restriction \(0\le f(x)\le1\) is required at every one of the \(2^n\) sign vectors. No range condition away from this cube is imposed.

Uniform averages and Fourier coefficients. For any real-valued function \(h\) on the cube, define \(\mathbb E h=2^{-n}\sum_{x\in\{-1,1\}^n}h(x)\). The characters \(\chi_S\) give the unique multilinear representation on the cube, with
\[\widehat f(S)=\mathbb E[f(x)\chi_S(x)]=a_S.\]
In particular \(\widehat f(\varnothing)=\mathbb Ef\). Variance is
\[\operatorname{Var}(f)=\mathbb E[(f-\mathbb Ef)^2]=\sum_{\varnothing\ne S\subseteq[n]}\widehat f(S)^2.\]
For the stated range, \(0\le\operatorname{Var}(f)\le1/4\).

Influence. Let \(x^{\oplus i}\) be obtained from \(x\) by negating its \(i\)-th coordinate and leaving all others fixed. Set
\[D_if(x)=\frac{f(x)-f(x^{\oplus i})}{2},\qquad \operatorname{Inf}_i(f)=\mathbb E[(D_if)^2]=\frac14\mathbb E[(f(x)-f(x^{\oplus i}))^2]=\sum_{S\ni i}\widehat f(S)^2.\]
This is a mean squared difference, not the probability that the two function values differ, their mean absolute difference, or the maximum change over inputs. All sums and expectations in the target use this same uniform measure.

Scope and quantifiers. Coefficients are arbitrary real numbers, without a rationality, description-length or computability restriction. The statement is an existence inequality, not a demand for an algorithm finding the coordinate. The coordinate may depend on the whole polynomial. No sparsity, block decomposition, common coefficient magnitude, Boolean-output, nonnegativity-of-coefficients or realizability-by-quantum-algorithms promise is present. There is no positive lower threshold on variance. Constant polynomials have zero variance and all influences zero, so every coordinate satisfies the inequality for them. The degree parameter is a positive upper bound, so division by zero never occurs.

Normalization of the exponent. Allowing any real \(C\ge1\) gives an equivalent assertion: for \(0\le v/d\le1/4\), increasing the exponent to a positive integer only decreases the right-hand side. A bound of the usual form \(c\,\operatorname{Var}(f)^a/d^b\), with fixed positive constants \(c,a,b\), also yields this formulation after increasing \(C\). Thus the one-exponent statement records polynomial dependence without selecting a particular best exponent or a hidden constant depending on \(n\).
cards.answer_criterion:
Give a complete mathematically correct proof checked in Lean of the universal existence claim or its negation. A positive answer must prove one exponent works simultaneously for every allowed \(n,d,f\), including arbitrarily small positive variance. No optimal exponent or algorithm for computing an influential coordinate is required.

A negative answer must prove that for every positive integer \(C\) there exist integers \(n\ge1\), \(1\le d\le n\), and an admissible polynomial of positive variance such that
\[\forall i\in[n],\quad\operatorname{Inf}_i(f)<\left(\frac{\operatorname{Var}(f)}d\right)^C.\]
The dimension, degree and polynomial may depend on \(C\). A rigorously specified family with those properties qualifies; a counterexample to just one proposed exponent does not negate the existence of another universal exponent. Numerical estimates must be certified strongly enough to establish the exact pointwise range and strict influence inequalities they assert.

A theorem only for Boolean-valued outputs, completely bounded forms, boundedly many quantum-query rounds, or a positive fraction of randomly restricted functions does not by itself cover the full polynomial class. An exponential dependence on degree is also weaker than the requested polynomial bound. This is a yes-or-no conjecture with an exact inequality, not a numerical target subject to additive 1/100 tolerance.
cards.why: A central structural question about real-valued Boolean-cube functions, with direct consequences for when quantum query algorithms can have large classical simulation costs.

importance.reason: Connects a basic dimension-independent influence bound to almost-everywhere classical simulation of quantum queries, bringing Boolean analysis and quantum complexity together.

progress.text: Aaronson–Ambainis formulate the influential-variable conjecture and prove its implication for almost-everywhere classical query simulation.
Keller–Klein withdraw their claimed general proof; the arXiv notice identifies failure of Lemma 5.3.
Bansal–Sinha–de Wolf establish the conjectured behavior for completely bounded block-multilinear forms.
Bhattacharya proves junta approximation after random restrictions and influential-variable guarantees for a non-negligible fraction of restrictions.
Revision 2 of the random-restriction preprint updates presentation and references while retaining its restriction and variance hypotheses.
Blanc–Docter–Strassle–Tan prove almost-everywhere simulation for bounded-round quantum algorithms, with a round-dependent polynomial exponent.
Escudero Gutiérrez–Saucedo–Palazuelos sharpen completely bounded block-multilinear root-influence bounds to the optimal constant and obtain nonadaptive simulation in that setting.

cards.status_note: Checked through 16 September 2026. The September 4 primary paper expressly leaves the unrestricted Aaronson–Ambainis conjecture open. Its sharper inequality uses a completely bounded block norm; the August simulation theorem has a round-dependent exponent, and the March random-restriction revision retains its variance and restriction hypotheses. The 2019 general proof claim remains withdrawn. No matching unrestricted resolution was found in the bounded primary-source search; external proofs were not independently formalized.

context_blocks.text: A low-degree polynomial contains interactions among only a few variables at a time, yet it may involve a very large number of variables overall. The question asks whether its variation must be detectably concentrated on at least one coordinate. The desired lower bound depends on the interaction degree and on how much the function varies, while having no dependence on the ambient number n of input bits.

Dependence on variance is essential. Consider \(f(x)=1/2+(x_{1}+\cdots +x_{n})/(2n)\). This degree-one polynomial always lies in \([0,1]\), but \(\operatorname{Var}(f)=1/(4n)\) and each coordinate has influence \(1/(4n^{2})\). No positive lower bound depending only on degree could work. The example is consistent with the conjectured polynomial dependence on variance. It also distinguishes an influential coordinate relative to the function’s variation from a coordinate with a constant absolute influence.

A \(t\)-query quantum algorithm has acceptance probability represented on the Boolean cube by a real polynomial of degree at most \(2t\), with values in \([0,1]\). Aaronson and Ambainis prove that the influence conjecture would imply a classical estimate of this probability within additive \(\varepsilon\) on at least a \(1-\eta\) fraction of uniformly distributed inputs using \(\operatorname{poly}(t,1/\varepsilon,1/\eta)\) queries. The classical algorithm may depend on the quantum algorithm. This gives a concrete reason why a dimension-independent inequality for bounded polynomials matters to quantum computation.

That consequence concerns query complexity. It does not automatically supply polynomial-time classical computation between queries, nor does it promise accurate simulation on every input. A small exceptional set can contain the entire promise domain of a quantum speedup. Also, the influential-variable conjecture is stronger than the simulation statement it implies: not every bounded low-degree polynomial is the acceptance probability of a quantum algorithm with a comparable query budget.

The distinction between bounded real outputs and Boolean outputs is substantial. The conjectured polynomial behavior is known for Boolean-valued functions, but the general real-valued case remains harder. Classical Fourier-analytic techniques yield bounds with exponential dependence on degree. These already force some influence, yet they do not provide the polynomial guarantee needed here.

Complete boundedness imposes more than scalar boundedness. In a block-multilinear polynomial, each monomial contains at most one variable from each of several fixed blocks. Replace variables by square matrix contractions, meaning matrices whose Euclidean operator norm is at most one, and multiply factors in block order. The completely bounded norm is the supremum of the resulting operator norm over all such matrices and dimensions. Requiring this norm to be at most one can support influential-variable theorems, but it is an extra hypothesis not imposed on the polynomials in this card.

The published ITCS 2025 restriction theorem assumes \(d\ge2\) and \(\operatorname{Var}(f)\ge1/d\). Each coordinate is independently left free with probability \(\log(d)/(C_1d)\), and otherwise fixed to an independent uniform sign. For universal positive constants \(C_1,C_2\), the resulting function has a coordinate with influence at least \(\operatorname{Var}(f)^2/d^{C_2}\) with probability at least \(\operatorname{Var}(f)\log(d)/(50C_1d)\). These are influences of the restricted function. The March 2026 revision retains both the restriction and original-variance assumptions; it does not establish the unrestricted claim.

Blanc, Docter, Strassle and Tan’s August 2026 theorem concerns quantum query rounds. A round applies parallel input queries between input-independent operations; the number \(r\) of rounds is distinct from the total \(t\) queries and from polynomial degree. Their classical query bound is \(2^{O(r^2)}(t\log(1/\eta)/\varepsilon)^{O(r)}\) for approximation error \(\varepsilon\) outside an \(\eta\) fraction of inputs. This is polynomial for fixed \(r\), but its exponent is not uniform over an unbounded number of rounds. The theorem neither treats every scalar bounded polynomial nor proves the full influential-variable conjecture.

The September 2026 theorem gives \(\sum_i\sqrt{\operatorname{Inf}_i(a)}\le t\|a\|_{\mathrm{cb}}\) for a polynomial with \(t\) blocks, summed over all variables. The constant is optimal, and the result permits nonadaptive classical queries in the associated restricted simulation. The authors expressly retain the unrestricted scalar conjecture as open. A small scalar norm does not supply the completely bounded norm hypothesis, so this sharper inequality is not a general resolution.

The 2019 Keller–Klein preprint once claimed a general proof, but the authors withdrew it on 2 December after a flaw in Lemma 5.3 invalidated the argument. The original abstract still contains the affirmative claim; its withdrawal notice is the controlling status information. It is not evidence that the conjecture has been established.

sentences: The Aaronson–Ambainis conjecture concerns real multilinear polynomials whose values lie between zero and one on every point of the Boolean cube.
It asks for a variable whose mean squared influence is bounded below by a fixed power of variance divided by degree, independent of the number of variables.
The universal claim includes arbitrary real coefficients and arbitrarily small positive variance, with one normalization and one exponent throughout.
A complete Lean proof must establish that claim or provide violations for every proposed exponent, rather than only a particular numerical power.
The conjecture would imply almost-everywhere classical query simulation, while known random-restriction, bounded-round and completely bounded results leave its full scalar form unresolved.

source_formulation.text: The inherited ITCS 2025 Conjecture 4 and Aaronson–Ambainis’s original Conjecture 6 ask for polynomially large influence in terms of variance and inverse degree. This card preserves its full scalar-polynomial scope, output interval [0,1], uniform sign cube, squared L2 influence, category and importance 96. The original source uses the bit cube and omits the factor 1/4 in its influence; changing cube coordinates preserves degree and this fixed normalization factor is absorbed by the unspecified exponent. Restricting the exponent to positive integers is equivalent, not an additional mathematical restriction.

statement_review.notes: Preserved importance 96 and the unrestricted Aaronson–Ambainis scalar-polynomial conjecture. Rebuilt malformed Fourier and influence notation, gave finite uniform averages and exact multilinear semantics, fixed influence normalization, and made degree and small-variance cases explicit. Stated the complete Lean criterion and full all-exponents negation; integer exponents are equivalent to the inherited real-exponent formulation. Rechecked original and published restricted theorems, March revision, August bounded-round simulation, September root-influence bound and author withdrawal. Removed procedural simulation text in favor of the sourced consequence and its precise limitations.

checked_sources: Read Aaronson–Ambainis arXiv:0911.0996v3 introductory Conjecture 6, Theorems 7–9 and simulation context: output in [0,1], original domain {0,1}^N, influence without factor 1/4, and unspecified polynomial exponent. The inherited normalized sign-cube version is equivalent after constant rescaling; classical query simulation is an implication, not an established equivalence with quantum realizability.

Read Bansal–Sinha–de Wolf CCC 2022 primary PDF full introduction, Conjecture 2 and §1.1: scalar Boolean-valued case known, general exponential-in-degree bound, arbitrary matrix dimensions in completely bounded norm and a theorem for block-multilinear forms. Read the main theorem rather than treating the abstract’s quantum correspondence as an all-polynomial statement.

Read Bhattacharya official ITCS 2025 PDF full introduction, Theorems 1 and 5 and Conjecture 4. Verified official publication on 11 February 2025, LIPIcs 325, pp.17:1–17:21. Separately read TR24-035 revision 2 full introduction, definitions and Theorem 6.4: d>=2, original variance >=1/d, survival log(d)/(C1 d), and positive-probability influence conclusion for restricted functions.

Read Blanc et al. arXiv:2608.19158v1 full §§1–2, round definition and Theorem 1: 2^{O(r²)}(t log(1/delta)/epsilon)^{O(r)} classical queries. The August 19 submission has an August 20 title-page date. The number of rounds is a separate parameter, and the exponent is not independent of it.

Read Escudero Gutiérrez–Saucedo–Palazuelos arXiv:2609.05201v1 full introduction, Conjecture 1.2, §1.1.1, Theorem 1.3, equations (5)–(6) and simulation corollary: sum of root influences <= number-of-blocks times completely bounded norm. This concerns block-ordered matrix substitutions, not the unrestricted scalar supremum norm. The September text explicitly leaves the general conjecture open.

Read current official arXiv:1911.03748v2 withdrawal notice, dated 2 December 2019: Lemma 5.3 fails to establish its claimed assertion. Do not promote the stale affirmative abstract. Screened August arXiv:2608.04411v2 primary abstract: operator/Pauli-string quantum inequalities are separate from this scalar-polynomial claim. Bounded searches through 16 September found no matching general resolution.

Checked finite Fourier normalization, example f=1/2+sum(x_i)/(2n), zero variance and positive degree, arbitrary real coefficients, quantifier dependencies and exact negation over all exponents. The candidate integer exponent is equivalent because Var/d<=1/4; changing the fixed prefactor does not change polynomial boundedness. No archived card body was read and external proofs were not independently formalized.

methodology: Detailed cards have individually written statements, context, significance, and documented results. Source notes are unfinished research records and do not yet meet that standard. The legacy index is retained for traceability.
Open in the source means open at the date of that source. The build date, 10 September 2026, does not establish current open status. Old excerpts may omit conditions or subsequent results.

Selection considers model power, necessary resources, sharp bounds, structural characterizations, explicit constructions, and minimal assumptions. Source notes use a heuristic screen; detailed cards give an individual explanation.

The earlier automatic paper screen allowed at most one new card per paper title and rejected identical formulations and close duplicates within a source. Approved textbook and survey imports retain multiple distinct questions per publication. Confirmed overlaps supplement existing cards; collection-wide semantic deduplication remains incomplete.

Short quotations retain the source language. Later related literature, where listed, is a research aid rather than evidence of resolution. Personal notes and saved cards are stored locally in your browser.

Textbook and survey questions are dated paraphrases; source locations, conjectures, research directions and caveats are preserved on the problem cards. These annotations do not establish current open status or change a later card review. New source drafts remain unassessed for importance. The reader contains the imported questions and external bibliographic references only; source files are not bundled.

Selection groups follow the agreed 10 large and 25 small categories. Our primary goal is a benchmark of 500 problems. Top 100 is a priority subset of those same 500, with secondary editorial attention. Both use the same category order and the same ranking within each category. The existing Top 1000 view is not an active benchmark goal. The respective prefixes are 5/2, 25/10 and 50/20 problems per large/small category. The legacy Top 1000 view has 1000 assigned places and 0 reserved places. Each card records its category explicitly. These counts describe saved candidates; classification does not verify a statement or its current open status. Inactive records are archived outside the catalogue, exports and editorial work. Their content, stable IDs and reasons are retained; imports cannot reactivate them. Final quota selection and a comprehensive deduplication audit remain pending.

Importance ordering is an editorial assessment of foundational significance, breadth of consequences, and influence on other questions. Each assessed card gives a reason. The category-wide review also uses shared priority bands for questions of comparable scope; it does not claim that these ties have a scientifically meaningful internal order. Unassessed drafts share a provisional score of 50; their relative order is only an ID tie-break, not an importance judgment. The first 5/2 places in each large/small category are an explicit editorial focus selection balancing importance and topical diversity. Focus ordering does not alter importance scores; remaining candidates use score and ID order. The primary target is 500 problems; Top 100 is its priority subset with secondary editorial attention. Top 100, Top 500 and the legacy Top 1000 view use the first 5/2, 25/10 and 50/20 category places respectively, all from the same ranking. Category positions include all candidates and remain fixed when filtering. Publication date, source date, and card detail do not increase importance. Inactive cards, including resolved records, are archived outside the ranking without changing their historical importance score. Importance review does not establish that a saved question is still open.
